note: Agents that were already on the list when the watch was written. They are not news: the block list is a decision already taken (docs/04 section 6). `loremfile crawler-watch` reports names that are neither here nor blocked; docs/04 section 6 says which are blocked without asking and which go to the reviewer. `deferred` holds names weighed and deliberately not blocked yet, each with its reasons and what would reopen it; the watch treats them as weighed.

reasons: Substring: a case-sensitive contains "nbot" also matches Amazonbot and msnbot, so the clause would reach a search engine's crawler (docs/04 section 6, first guard).
No published user agent: NBot (nbot.ai) publishes none, so neither the exact string nor its casing is known, and a clause in the list's lower case might never fire.
nbot.reopen: When NBot publishes an exact user-agent string: block it with an exact match on that string rather than contains (ADR-033).

reasons: Substring: at three characters a case-sensitive contains "Dot" also matches Moz's link-index crawler, which Moz spells DotBot in its page title and Dotbot in its prose (moz.com/help/moz-procedures/crawlers/dotbot, read 2026-10-26), so the clause would reach a crawler this group is not aimed at (docs/04 section 6, first guard).

No published user agent: the list gives Dot no operator and OpenAI's crawler page names only OAI-SearchBot, OAI-AdsBot, GPTBot and ChatGPT-User (read 2026-10-26), so neither an exact string nor a casing is known.
Dot.reopen: When an exact user-agent string is published for Dot: block it with an exact match on that string rather than contains (ADR-033).

reasons: Display name, not a product token: the name contains whitespace, and RFC 9309 section 2.2.1 confines the robots.txt product token to letters, underscores and hyphens, so no User-agent: line can carry it and a case-sensitive contains clause would fire only on a user agent holding the name with its space (docs/04 section 6, third guard).
AGI Agent.reopen: When the operator publishes a product token without whitespace, or an exact user-agent string: weigh that token under the standing rule, or block the exact string with an exact match rather than contains (ADR-033).
